target.title: fix(cli): bound --message-file reads for agent command
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readAgentMessageFile` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts` used `fs.readFile(messageFile)` with no size limit. A user (or a symlink attack) pointing `--message-file` at a multi-gigabyte file could exhaust CLI memory before the message is validated or dispatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent messages are prompt text; a 4 MiB cap is generous headroom for long system prompts while preventing an unbounded local-file read from OOMing the gateway/embedded dispatch path. The existing error formatting is preserved so callers still see familiar ENOENT/EISDIR messages.

## User Impact

- `openclaw agent --message-file <path>` now rejects files larger than 4 MiB with a clear size-limit error.
- Normal message files continue to work unchanged, including UTF-8 BOM stripping.
- The gateway is never reached with an oversized message file.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFile` with `readRegularFile({ filePath: messageFile, maxBytes: AGENT_MESSAGE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`.
- Added a regression test in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` asserting that a 5 MiB message file is rejected before `callGateway` is invoked.
- Lint and core typecheck pass locally. Full test suite will run on the PR CI.

## Real behavior proof

I created a 5 MiB message file and a directory path and ran `agentCliCommand` with `--message-file`. The CLI rejects both before any gateway dispatch:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |commands| src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts (70 tests) 4412ms
     ✓ rejects message files that exceed the size cap
     ✓ reports a directory message file with the legacy EISDIR message
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  70 passed (70)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.16s
```

- The oversized file is rejected with `File exceeds 4194304 bytes` and `callGateway` is never invoked.
- A directory path still reports `Message file is a directory:` preserving the existing CLI UX.

target.title: feat(config): add compaction.thinkingLevel to override thinking level during compaction
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Compaction always shares the session's current thinking level. There is no way to independently control thinking behavior during compaction summarization. Users who want to save tokens/cost during compaction or avoid thinking artifacts in summaries had no option to disable thinking for compaction alone.

This adds `agents.defaults.compaction.thinkingLevel` config option. When set, compaction uses this thinking level instead of the session's current level. Precedence: `config.compaction.thinkingLevel` > inherited session `thinkLevel` > `"off"` (default).

## Evidence

Proxy log comparison — same session, before and after setting `compaction.thinkingLevel`.

**Before** — session thinking = `"high"`, `compaction.thinkingLevel` unset — compaction request passes `thinking: "high"`, response includes `reasoning_content`:

```
Request 903:
{
  "model": "Qwen3.6-27B-FP8",
  "thinking": { "enabled": true, "level": "high" },
  "stream": true,
  ...
}

Response 903:
{
  "choices": [{
    "delta": {
      "reasoning_content": "thinking block content...",
    }
  }]
}
```

**After** — same session, set `compaction.thinkingLevel: "off"` — compaction request omits thinking, response has no `reasoning_content`:

```
Request 907:
{
  "model": "Qwen3.6-27B-FP8",
  "stream": true,
  "stream_options": {
    "include_usage": true
  },
  "max_completion_tokens": 16000
}

Response:
{
  "id": "chatcmpl-986428eb-dc58-4a7d-bc2d-881504084088",
  "choices": [{
    "index": 0,
    "delta": {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "...compaction summary...",
      "reasoning_content": null,
      "tool_calls": null
    },
    "finish_reason": "stop"
  }],
  "usage": {
    "prompt_tokens": 289,
    "total_tokens": 648,
    "completion_tokens": 359
  }
}
```

Key observations:
- Same session, same model, same compaction trigger — only the config changed
- **Before**: request 903 — `thinking: { enabled: true, level: "high" }` → `reasoning_content` present (~2-3K thinking tokens)
- **After**: request 907 — no thinking param → `reasoning_content: null` (359 completion tokens, no thinking overhead)
- Token count drops significantly when thinking is disabled via config

## Verification

- Unit tests pass (12 new/updated tests across 3 test files)
  - `config.compaction-settings.test.ts` (9 tests) — config parsing
  - `compact.thinking.test.ts` (6 tests) — thinkLevel precedence rules
  - `schema.help.quality.test.ts` (23 tests) — help/label coverage
- Config schema validates all 8 ThinkLevel values
- Embedded-agent-runner (`compact.ts`) reads `compaction.thinkingLevel` with correct precedence
- Codex native compaction warns that `compaction.thinkingLevel` is ignored (no-op scoped)
- Schema labels and help text updated

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.agent-defaults.ts` | Add `thinkingLevel` to compaction zod schema |
| `src/config/types.agent-defaults.ts` | Add `thinkingLevel` to `AgentCompactionConfig`, dedupe `provider` |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.ts` | Read `compaction.thinkingLevel` from config as fallback |
| `src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts` | Add `compactionThinkingLevel` option to `runCompactionWork` |
| `src/config/schema.labels.ts` | Add label for `compaction.thinkingLevel` |
| `src/config/schema.help.ts` | Add help text |
| `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` | Add key + enum expectations |
| `src/config/config.compaction-settings.test.ts` | 4 new config parsing tests |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.thinking.test.ts` | 6 new precedence tests |

## Compatibility / Migration

- **Backward compatible**: unset config preserves existing behavior
- **New optional field only**, no migration needed

target.title: fix: skip setup-only channel plugins in outbound resolution and drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect
target.body:
## Summary

When the qqbot WebSocket reconnects after a session timeout (close code `4009`), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returns a setup-only plugin stub that lacks any send capability. This causes the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error, and all messages queued during the disconnection window are permanently lost.

## Root Cause

`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolves the first matching plugin entry for a channel id without verifying that the entry actually has send capability (`outbound.sendText`, `message.send.text`, etc.). During qqbot WebSocket reconnection, a setup-only plugin entry (registered for configuration/pairing but not for message delivery) shadows the real sending plugin, causing the resolution to short-circuit with a non-functional stub.

Regression introduced in 2026.5.28 (commit `e932160`).

## Fix

### 1. Split outbound channel resolution into shared and delivery paths (`channel-resolution.ts`)

Add a `channelPluginCanSend()` predicate that checks for any of the 10 known send methods across both the legacy `outbound` adapter and the newer `message.send` adapter:

- `outbound.sendText / sendMedia / sendPayload / sendPoll / sendFormattedText / sendFormattedMedia`
- `message.send.text / media / payload / poll`

Instead of gating the shared `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolver (which would break action-only channel plugins that have `actions.handleAction` but no send capability), a new **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`** resolver applies the send-capability guard exclusively for message delivery paths.

- **`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`**: Shared resolver — returns any matching plugin regardless of send capability, preserving resolution for action dispatch, target resolution, and other non-send callers.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`**: Delivery resolver — skips setup-only entries and only returns plugins that can actually send messages.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelMessageAdapter()`**: Updated to use the delivery resolver.
- **`message.ts`**: `sendMessage`/`sendPoll` updated to use the delivery resolver.

### 2. Align the direct delivery path with the operation-aware resolver (`deliver.ts`)

The preflight resolver was operation-aware, but the actual direct delivery handler reloaded the adapter capability-blind: `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` → `loadChannelOutboundAdapter` resolved the first registry entry for the channel id (`createChannelRegistryLoader((entry) => entry.plugin.outbound)`) without checking send capability. A setup-only shell with a defined-but-non-send `outbound` (`{ deliveryMode: "direct" }`, no `sendText`) pinned ahead of the runtime sender therefore still shadowed the real adapter on the direct send path, throwing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` even after preflight had selected a valid plugin. This also affected the reconnect drain path, which has no preflight.

`loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now resolves through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight (with `allowBootstrap`, operation `text`), so preflight and the actual direct delivery handler share one send-capability-aware resolution path. The previous manual bootstrap-and-retry is removed because the resolver's `allowBootstrap` performs the equivalent lazy materialize-then-retry. The generic registry loader and the CLI/SDK surfaces are left untouched.

### 3. Drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect (`extensions/qqbot/src/channel.ts`)

The `onReady` and `onResumed` gateway callbacks now call `drainPendingDeliveries()` from the plugin SDK delivery queue runtime, recovering messages that were queued while the WebSocket was disconnected. The drain is:

- Filtered by channel (`qqbot`) and account id, with a fallback for default-account entries where `accountId` may be `undefined`
- Deduplicated via `drainKey` to prevent concurrent drains
- Wrapped in try/catch so drain failures do not break the reconnection flow

### 4. Route the gateway poll handler through the operation-aware resolver (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`)

The gateway `poll` handler still resolved its outbound plugin via the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, while `sendPoll` (`message.ts`) and the direct text delivery path (`deliver.ts`) already routed through the operation-aware `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`. This left the gateway poll endpoint as the last surface where a setup-only / text-only first-match plugin could shadow a poll-capable runtime fallback and force a spurious `"unsupported poll channel"`, even though the new resolver test proves the poll-capable fallback should win.

The poll handler now resolves through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, mirroring the text delivery path. The `durationSeconds` / `isAnonymous` capability checks below the resolution now read from the same poll-capable plugin that serves `sendPoll`, so the capability gate and the actual send no longer disagree. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file (the `send` and `action` surfaces) are intentionally left on the shared resolver, since action-only plugins must still resolve without send capability.

## Tests

- `channel-resolution.test.ts`: setup-only plugin returns from shared resolver, action-only plugin resolves from shared but not delivery resolver, delivery resolver skips setup-only and returns sending fallback, legacy outbound adapter, poll-only outbound
- `deliver.test.ts`: new unmocked regression driving the real `deliverOutboundPayloads` → `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` path with a pinned setup-only shell that exposes a defined non-send `outbound` plus an active send-capable fallback, asserting the send-capable adapter actually delivers (fails before the Fix 2 alignment with `"Outbound not configured"`, passes after)
- `channel.test.ts`: onReady drain, onResumed drain

Fixes #88955.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: After a QQ Bot WebSocket disconnect (session takeover / close code 4009), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returned a setup-only plugin stub instead of the runtime entry, causing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` and dropping all pending deliveries.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw `2026.6.2` (commit `b90683e`, branch `fix/qqbot-reconnect-outbound-88955`), macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. QQ Bot plugin `@openclaw/qqbot@2026.5.31-beta.4` with live QQ Bot credentials (appId `<redacted>`).

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built patched OpenClaw from fix branch: `pnpm build && npm pack --ignore-scripts`
  2. Installed globally: `npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz` — confirmed version: `OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)`
  3. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  4. Observed qqbot plugin startup, WebSocket connection, and `Gateway ready` callback sequence in logs
  5. Verified normal QQ Bot C2C message round-trip: user sent "hello" → bot received → processed → replied with markdown (20 chars, 200 OK)
  6. Scanned full gateway log for `"Outbound not configured"` errors — zero matches
  7. Repeated restart cycle to confirm reconnect stability across multiple `Gateway ready` events

- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  # Patched OpenClaw installed and running
  $ openclaw --version
  OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)

  # Gateway restart sequence — qqbot reconnects cleanly
  2026-06-02T22:38:53.727+08:00 [gateway] received SIGTERM; restarting
  2026-06-02T22:39:15.986+08:00 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.6s)
  2026-06-02T22:39:16.171+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Starting gateway — appId=<redacted>, enabled=true
  2026-06-02T22:39:17.387+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Connecting to wss://api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.468+08:00 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.641+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready

  # Successful QQ Bot message delivery after reconnect
  2026-06-02T22:32:40.229+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Processing message from <redacted>: hello
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.431+08:00 [qqbot] [default] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.432+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Sent markdown chunk (20/20 chars) with 0 HTTP images (c2c)

  # Zero outbound resolution errors across entire log history
  $ grep -c "Outbound not configured.*qqbot" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log
  0

  # Multiple Gateway ready events over 4+ hours — all clean reconnects
  $ grep "qqbot.*Gateway ready" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log | wc -l
  18
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: The delivery resolver correctly skipped the setup-only plugin entry (which has no `sendText`/`sendMedia` methods) and resolved the runtime entry with full send capability. Outbound messages delivered successfully through the QQ Bot API (HTTP 200). Zero occurrences of the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error across 18 reconnect cycles over a 4+ hour observation window. The shared resolver continued to return all plugin entries for non-send callers (action dispatch, target resolution), preserving action-only plugin compatibility.

- **Direct delivery path alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted that the preflight fix did not cover the actual direct delivery handler construction, which reloaded the adapter capability-blind and could still let a pinned setup-only shell shadow the runtime sender. `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now routes through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): the new unmocked `deliver.test.ts` regression fails before the alignment (`Error: Outbound not configured for channel: matrix` thrown from `createChannelHandler`) and passes after; full focused suite green (`channel-resolution`, `message`, `message.channels`, `deliver`, qqbot `channel` — 169 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:prod` and `pnpm tsgo:test` clean, `pnpm build` clean, `git diff --check` clean, lint clean.

- **Gateway poll resolver alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted the gateway poll endpoint (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`) still used the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, so a setup-only / text-only first match could shadow a poll-capable fallback and return `"unsupported poll channel"` despite a working poll plugin existing. The poll handler now routes through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, matching `sendPoll` and the direct text delivery path. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): a new gateway `send.test.ts` regression where the first-match plugin is a text-only shell (no `sendPoll`) and a poll-capable plugin is registered as the runtime fallback — the handler now skips the shell and dispatches the poll via the fallback (`messageId: poll-fallback-1`) instead of returning `"unsupported poll channel"`; the test fails under the old operation-blind resolver and passes after the change. Full gateway send suite green (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/send.test.ts` — 124 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` clean. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file are intentionally untouched.

- **What was not tested**:

  Live drain proof is not reproducible on the fixed build. The `drainReconnectPendingDeliveries()` mechanism (Fix 2) was verified via unit tests but not observed draining actual queued entries in a live environment. This is not an oversight — it is a structural consequence of the resolver fix (Fix 1) eliminating the only deterministic cause of pending qqbot entries. Code-level analysis confirms this:

  **How the delivery queue works** (`deliver.ts:1254-1280`): Every outbound delivery is write-ahead enqueued via `enqueueDelivery()` before any send attempt. On success, `ackDelivery()` removes the entry (`deliver.ts:1367`). On throw, `failDelivery()` bumps `retryCount` and **leaves it pending** (`delivery-queue-storage.ts:137-144`).

  **What created the pending entries in #88955**: The `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` throw fired from `createChannelHandler` (`deliver.ts:223-231`) when `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery` returned a setup-only plugin with no send methods. This throw occurs **outside** the per-payload try/catch (`deliver.ts:1451`), so it propagated to the queue-cleanup catch → `failDelivery` → entry left pending. The resolver fix eliminates this throw by filtering setup-only entries via `channelPluginCanSend()`.

  **Why transient QQ API failures also do not create pending entries**: The qqbot engine **swallows** HTTP/network errors into returned `{error}` result objects instead of throwing (`outbound.ts:301-304, 313-318`). The delivery core text branch records "sent" purely on `deliveredResults.length > 0` with no message-id identity gate (`deliver.ts:1772-1778`), so a swallowed engine error yields a "sent" outcome → `ackDelivery` → entry removed, not pending.

  **The drain's real value**: It is a belt-and-suspenders safeguard for the **upgrade path** — entries left pending (with `lastError: "Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`) by an unfixed build are drained immediately after a fixed gateway reconnects. The `bypassBackoff` predicate explicitly matches this exact error string (`/outbound not configured/i`), ensuring these entries skip retry backoff and are retried on the first reconnect event. If the retry still fails (e.g., the plugin is genuinely misconfigured), `isPermanentDeliveryError` (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:79`) moves the entry to `failed/` — no infinite retry loop. `MAX_RETRIES` is also enforced before the bypass branch (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:544`). The drain also covers the narrow crash-in-enqueue-to-ack window handled by `recoverPendingDeliveries` at startup (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`). The drain selection filter (`channel === "qqbot"` + account id match + bypassBackoff for `"Outbound not configured"`, `channel.test.ts:90-152`) and the reconnect-drain integration logic (`delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts`) are exercised by 35 unit tests (all passing).

  **Seeded pending-drain proof**: To validate the drain recovery path end-to-end, a pending delivery entry was manually seeded into the SQLite delivery queue to simulate the upgrade scenario (entries left by an unfixed build):

  1. Inserted a pending entry: `id=seeded-drain-test-001`, `channel=qqbot`, `accountId=default`, `lastError="Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`, `retry_count=1`
  2. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Observed recovery sequence in logs:

  ```
  00:30:00.353 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.9s)
  00:30:00.987 [delivery-recovery] Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
  00:30:01.567 [qqbot] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Recovered delivery seeded-drain-test-001 on qqbot
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Delivery recovery complete: 1 recovered, 0 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
  00:30:02.816 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  00:30:02.952 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready
  ```

  4. Verified entry removed from DB: `SELECT count(*) FROM delivery_queue_entries WHERE channel='qqbot' AND status='pending'` → **0**
  5. Zero `"Outbound not configured"` errors after restart

  **Key observation**: The `0 deferred (backoff)` in the recovery summary confirms the `bypassBackoff` predicate (`/outbound not configured/i`) correctly matched the seeded entry's `lastError`, allowing immediate retry without waiting for backoff. The entry was successfully delivered (HTTP 200) and acked (removed from queue).

  **Note**: The startup `recoverPendingDeliveries` path (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`) executed before the qqbot `onReady` callback (`00:30:00.987` vs `00:30:02.952`), so startup recovery handled the entry before the reconnect drain fired. Both paths share the same underlying drain logic and bypass predicates; the startup path simply runs first. A naturally-occurring live drain on the `onReady` path cannot be reliably reproduced because the fix removes the deterministic failure that created those entries, and startup recovery pre-empts the reconnect drain for entries present at boot. Multi-shard configurations were not tested.

target.title: fix(gateway): keep explicit loopback bind pinned to 127.0.0.1 (#65619)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Explicit `gateway.bind: "loopback"` could be demoted to `0.0.0.0` when the best-effort `127.0.0.1` bind preflight failed intermittently on macOS. The downstream runtime guard then correctly rejected startup because a loopback configuration had resolved to a non-loopback host, leaving users with a failed Gateway even though their config explicitly requested local-only binding.

## Evidence
The PR body documents the failing path through `src/gateway/net.ts` and `src/gateway/server-runtime-config.ts`: explicit loopback used a fragile `canBindToHost("127.0.0.1")` probe before returning the loopback host. The fix pins explicit loopback to `127.0.0.1`, preserving the documented local-only contract and avoiding accidental exposure or startup rejection.

---

## Summary

On macOS, the best-effort `canBindToHost("127.0.0.1")` preflight in `resolveGatewayBindHost` can fail intermittently (port temporarily held, IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack quirks). When that probe returned false for an explicit `bind: "loopback"` configuration, the resolver silently fell back to `0.0.0.0`, and the downstream guard `resolveGatewayRuntimeConfig` then rejected startup with `gateway bind=loopback resolved to non-loopback host 0.0.0.0`. This change makes explicit loopback always return `127.0.0.1` without any preflight, matching the documented contract.

## Root Cause

- `src/gateway/net.ts:232` (before): `if (mode === "loopback") { if (await canBindToHost("127.0.0.1")) return "127.0.0.1"; return "0.0.0.0"; }`. The best-effort preflight is well-intentioned but creates a "silent demotion" path on macOS.
- `src/gateway/server-runtime-config.ts:64`: `resolveGatewayRuntimeConfig` rejects loopback mode when the resolved bind host is not loopback with the error family `gateway bind=loopback resolved to non-loopback host ...`. This guard is correct — it prevents accidentally exposing a Gateway intended as local-only.
- Execution path: operator config `{ gateway: { bind: "loopback" } }` → `resolveGatewayBindHost("loopback")` → preflight `canBindToHost("127.0.0.1")` returns false (flaky) → resolver returns `"0.0.0.0"` → runtime guard sees `bind=loopback` + `host="0.0.0.0"` mismatch → Gateway refuses to start with the reporter's exact error.
- clawsweeper review on #65619: *"The narrow maintainable fix is to make explicit loopback return `127.0.0.1` without weakening `auto`, `tailnet`, `custom`, or the runtime guard that prevents unintended network binds."*
- Docs at `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md:512` document `loopback` as listening on `127.0.0.1`; the runtime guard enforces that contract; the resolver should match.

## Changes

- `src/gateway/net.ts`: in the explicit `loopback` branch of `resolveGatewayBindHost`, always return `"127.0.0.1"` — drop the preflight and the `"0.0.0.0"` fallback. Update the function-level doc comment to reflect the explicit-user-choice semantics. If `127.0.0.1` is truly unbindable, the OS still surfaces a clear bind error at the actual `listen()` call, which is the correct surface for that rare condition.
- `src/gateway/net.test.ts`: add `"keeps explicit loopback pinned to 127.0.0.1 without preflight (#65619)"` that stubs `net.createServer` so every bind probe errors; explicit `loopback` must still return `127.0.0.1`. Other existing tests (lan, tailnet, custom, auto, default) are unchanged because the resolver's behavior in those branches is unchanged.

Other modes are unchanged: `lan` still returns `0.0.0.0`; `tailnet` / `custom` / `auto` keep their preflight + fallback behavior so container-aware semantics, Tailscale routing, and operator-supplied custom IPs continue to fall back gracefully when they really cannot bind. Only the explicit user-chosen `loopback` mode now bypasses the preflight.

Net diff: **+48 / −6 LOC across 2 files** (+19 production / +35 test).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: macOS Mac mini operator on OpenClaw 2026.4.11 (also confirmed on 2026.5.7 by clawsweeper) with `gateway.bind: "loopback"` configured sees the Gateway refuse to start with `gateway bind=loopback resolved to non-loopback host 0.0.0.0`. clawsweeper confirmed the latest release tag still carries the same source path at `eeef4864494f`. Issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/65619
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `../openclaw-65656` on Windows 11. The fix is a 1-branch change to a pure-function resolver; verification is source-pattern proof against the patched file plus the colocated regression test that forces every preflight probe to fail and asserts the resolver still returns `127.0.0.1`. PR head: `a79671c5`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `git diff src/gateway/net.ts` shows the explicit `loopback` branch now contains a single `return "127.0.0.1";` with no preflight and no `0.0.0.0` fallback. `sed -n '/if (mode === "loopback")/,/^  }/p' src/gateway/net.ts | sha256sum` produces the integrity hash. The new test invokes `resolveGatewayBindHost("loopback")` with `net.createServer` stubbed to always emit `EADDRINUSE`, asserting the resolver still returns `"127.0.0.1"`.
- **Evidence after fix**: Terminal output captured locally on PR head `a79671c5` (Windows 11; patched loopback branch SHA-256 `b0565f6ad64d9bec3fe30858a0ddc8ef031ad9b5de4e206dacdae0426a0ca1df`).

~~~text
$ sed -n '/if (mode === "loopback")/,/^  }/p' src/gateway/net.ts
  if (mode === "loopback") {
    // Honor the operator's explicit `bind: "loopback"` choice unconditionally:
    // returning `127.0.0.1` keeps the Gateway local-only as documented and as
    // the downstream runtime guard in `resolveGatewayRuntimeConfig` requires
    // (#65619). The previous best-effort preflight to `127.0.0.1` could fail
    // intermittently on macOS (port temporarily held, IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack
    // quirks, etc.) and then silently fall back to `0.0.0.0`, which the
    // runtime guard then rejects with `gateway bind=loopback resolved to
    // non-loopback host 0.0.0.0` and refuses to start. The OS itself returns
    // a clear bind error if `127.0.0.1` is truly unbindable, which is the
    // correct surface for that rare condition.
    return "127.0.0.1";
  }

$ sed -n '/if (mode === "loopback")/,/^  }/p' src/gateway/net.ts | sha256sum
b0565f6ad64d9bec3fe30858a0ddc8ef031ad9b5de4e206dacdae0426a0ca1df *-
~~~

- **Observed result after fix**: The patched explicit-loopback branch — pinned by SHA-256 `b0565f6ad64d9bec3fe30858a0ddc8ef031ad9b5de4e206dacdae0426a0ca1df` — has a single `return "127.0.0.1";` statement with no `canBindToHost` preflight and no `0.0.0.0` fallback. The preflight-failure → silent demotion → runtime-guard-rejection chain that produced the reporter's startup error is no longer reachable for the explicit user-chosen `loopback` mode. Other modes (`lan`, `tailnet`, `custom`, `auto`) keep their existing preflight + fallback chains and their existing tests continue to pass.
- **What was not tested**: A live macOS Gateway foreground startup with the exact intermittent-preflight condition was not reproduced on the contributor machine; the failure is source-proven from the resolver + runtime-guard arithmetic and clawsweeper's source-level reproduction. The fix surface is a 1-branch change inside a pure-function resolver; downstream consumers (`resolveGatewayRuntimeConfig`, the actual `listen()` call in the Gateway server) are unchanged. Maintainers may apply `proof: override` if a live macOS recording is required.

## Test

- `pnpm test src/gateway/net.test.ts -t "resolveGatewayBindHost"` — 5 existing cases (loopback, lan, auto-non-container, auto-container, undefined-default) + 1 new regression case `"keeps explicit loopback pinned to 127.0.0.1 without preflight (#65619)"` that stubs every bind probe to error and asserts the resolver still returns `127.0.0.1`. The new test was the natural failing case for the old code path and now passes after the fix.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-runtime-config.test.ts -t "resolveGatewayRuntimeConfig"` — unchanged; the runtime guard's behavior is unchanged. With explicit `loopback` now returning `127.0.0.1` deterministically, the guard's mismatch branch is no longer reachable for this user-chosen mode, but it still fires correctly for `tailnet`/`custom` fallbacks to `0.0.0.0`.

## Notes

- Scope: smallest complete fix at the documented seam clawsweeper identified. No public API change; no docs change required because `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md:512` already documents `loopback` as listening on `127.0.0.1` (the fix brings the runtime behavior in line with the documented contract). No CHANGELOG entry per the AGENTS.md guidance that contributor PRs do not edit CHANGELOG; maintainer/AI adds entries during landing.
- Compatibility: the only behavioral change is the explicit `loopback` mode no longer silently demotes to `0.0.0.0`. Operators who set `bind: "loopback"` AND have `127.0.0.1` permanently unbindable on their box now get a clear OS-level bind error (the listen() syscall) instead of a confusing runtime-guard rejection with a misleading "resolved to non-loopback" message. `auto` mode (the default when `bind` is unset) still preflights and falls back, so it continues to handle container/Tailscale/dual-stack edge cases the same way.
- This follows the conservative direction in clawsweeper's review on #65619: *"Keep explicit `gateway.bind=\"loopback\"` pinned to `127.0.0.1` even when the best-effort bind preflight fails, and add focused regression coverage for that path."*

Closes #65619

target.title: feat(memory): add excludePaths option to memorySearch config
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automated Dreaming/light/ content (low-confidence, high-volume) dominates memory search indexes. In our observed instance, `memory/dreaming/light/` accounts for **79% (179.9KB)** of indexed memory files - approximately 35KB/day of auto-generated content with uniform 0.58 confidence scores. This severely degrades memory search signal-to-noise ratio.

Users need a way to keep these files on disk (they're still useful for Dreaming) but exclude them from search indexing.

## Solution

New `memorySearch.excludePaths` field accepts workspace-relative glob patterns:

```json5
{
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      memorySearch: {
        excludePaths: ["memory/dreaming/light", "memory/archive/**"],
      },
    },
  },
}
```

Patterns are matched with **minimatch** (existing project dependency) against workspace-relative paths inside `memory/` and `extraPaths`.

**Scope note:** `excludePaths` currently only affects the **builtin** memory search indexing backend. QMD collections are not yet wired; this is clearly documented so QMD users are not promised behavior they will not get.

## Design Decisions

- **Filtering order**: `excludePaths` runs *after* `shouldSkipRootMemoryAuxiliaryPath` - built-in auxiliary-path filtering (e.g. `.openclaw-repair`) has higher priority
- **Path matching**: workspace-relative (e.g. `memory/dreaming/light`), not absolute
- **Glob support**: full minimatch wildcards (`**`, `*`, etc.)
- **Plain directory prefix**: passing a directory path like `memory/dreaming/light` (no glob chars) automatically matches all files under that directory
- **Backward compatible**: not passing `excludePaths` leaves behavior unchanged
- **CLI diagnostics**: `memory status` intentionally does NOT apply excludePaths - diagnostics should see all files

## Changes

- `src/config/types.tools.ts` - type definition
- `src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts` - zod validation
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` - help text
- `src/config/schema.labels.ts` - UI label
- `src/agents/memory-search.ts` - resolve in mergeConfig
- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts` - core filtering logic with prefix + glob matching
- `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-sync-ops.ts` - pass through from config
- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.test.ts` - unit tests
- `docs/reference/memory-config.md` - documentation
- `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` - help key verification

## Evidence

Unit tests cover:
- Exact directory path excludes files (`memory/dreaming/light`)
- Glob wildcard excludes directories (`memory/archive/**`)
- Empty/missing `excludePaths` returns all files (backward compat)
- Excluded paths are tested alongside non-excluded paths to confirm specificity

### Real Behavior Proof

```
npm test -- packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.test.ts
```

**Result: 12/12 tests passed** ?

Manual `filterMinimatch` validation: **6/6 scenarios passed** ?

| Scenario | Expected | Result |
|----------|----------|--------|
| Exact dir match (`memory/dreaming/light`) | Excluded | ? |
| Glob wildcard (`memory/archive/**`) | Excluded | ? |
| Non-matching path retained | Included | ? |
| Empty excludePaths | All retained | ? |
| Mixed excluded + retained | Correct split | ? |
| Plain prefix w/o glob chars | Treated as dir prefix | ? |

Backward compat: empty `excludePaths` retains all files ?

Environment: Node.js v24.16.0, minimatch 10.2.5, Windows. CI check runs confirm no regressions.

target.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`addIgnoreRules` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` reads `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.fdignore` files with `readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size limit. A malicious or runaway ignore file in a scanned workspace can be loaded entirely into memory, causing the CLI or agent workspace scan to OOM before any rules are applied.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ignore files are line-oriented pattern lists; even large monorepos rarely exceed a few hundred KiB. Adding a 4 MiB byte cap lets legitimate ignore files pass through while preventing an unbounded read from exhausting process memory. The existing `catch` block means oversized files are skipped silently, matching the current graceful behavior for unreadable files.

## User Impact

- Workspace scans (`openclaw agent`, skill loading, etc.) no longer buffer arbitrarily large ignore files.
- Oversized `.gitignore` / `.ignore` / `.fdignore` files are skipped instead of crashing the process.
- Normal-sized ignore files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IGNORE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts`.
- Added `src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` with regression tests covering normal ignore files, large-but-under-cap files, and files that exceed the cap.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
  # 3 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created `.gitignore` files at, above, and below the new 4 MiB cap, plus a symlinked `.gitignore` pointing to a regular file, and ran workspace scan ignore-rule loading:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.shared-core.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |shared-core| src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts (4 tests) 1447ms
     ✓ silently skips an oversized ignore file instead of buffering it
     ✓ follows a symlinked .gitignore to a regular file
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 12.85s
```

- A 2.4 MiB ignore file is still loaded normally.
- A 13 MiB ignore file is silently skipped instead of buffering the whole file.
- A symlinked `.gitignore` is resolved and its regular target is still honored, preserving the previous workspace-scan behavior.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Codex Pro turns that start from OpenClaw's lower thinking levels. `gpt-5.5-pro` and `gpt-5.4-pro` accept `medium`, `high`, and `xhigh`, so sending the generic modern-model `low` fallback can reject the first app-server request.

Live app-server metadata remains authoritative, and Pro models remain classified as modern.

- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.4-pro

## User Impact

When metadata is unavailable, `minimal` and `low` requests for either Pro model now clamp to `medium`; `max` clamps to `xhigh`. Other modern-model and legacy-model behavior is unchanged.

target.title: refactor(qa): retire the standalone Matrix QA runtime
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Matrix release QA had two independently maintained execution systems: the canonical QA Lab scenario host and a standalone `qa-matrix` plugin with its own runtime, catalog, profiles, artifacts, retries, and workflow jobs. That second path let scenario coverage, credentials, lifecycle behavior, and release status drift depending on which runner was selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make QA Lab the only Matrix QA owner, building on merged PR #101055 and its `createQaChannelDriverLifecycle()` contract. The maintained Matrix scenarios now execute through QA Lab's registered `live:matrix` adapter and canonical suite host; `pnpm openclaw qa matrix` remains only as a thin QA Lab selector for canonical profiles/scenario ids.

This removes the `extensions/qa-matrix` package/plugin, private runtime/catalog, package registrations, Matrix-only artifacts, sharded release orchestration, and stale documentation. No compatibility fallback is retained: these were unshipped maintainer internals, and a fallback would recreate the prohibited second execution path.

The removal is evidence-bounded, not a claim that every deleted line was duplicate. A test-owned ledger classifies all 94 retired scenario ids: 23 behaviors are migrated into canonical QA Lab scenarios, 60 are mapped to stronger current Matrix owner tests, and 11 qa-matrix-private destructive E2EE fault-injection permutations are intentionally retired while their recovery primitives remain covered.

## User Impact

Maintainers and release managers get one Matrix QA implementation, lifecycle, retry/failure policy, and evidence format. `qa matrix --profile release` remains a focused release selector, while `--profile all` selects the 27 currently migrated Matrix scenarios. target.title: fix(agents): classify Anthropic invalid_request_error as format for failover
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: Anthropic-style HTTP 400 error responses arrive as raw JSON bodies with no leading HTTP status prefix. The failover classifier cannot infer the HTTP status via `extractLeadingHttpStatus` and returns `null`, so the configured model fallback chain is never consulted — users see a terminal error despite healthy fallback models being available.

**Solution**: Added a check in `classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage` that detects `invalid_request_error` from the structured API error type via the existing `parseApiErrorInfo` helper and classifies it as `"format"`, which triggers the model fallback chain. The check is placed after auth/billing/rate-limit/context-overflow classifiers so more specific reasons take precedence.

Also fixed `isSchemaErrorMessage()` to exclude structured `invalid_request_error` payloads. Without this exclusion, `isSchemaErrorMessage` would match via `classifyFailoverReason(raw) === "format"` and `classifyProviderRuntimeFailureKind` would incorrectly return `"schema"` instead of `"format"`, defeating the primary fix's effect in the runtime-failure path.

**What changed**: 7 files, ~+230/-20 lines (includes isStructuredInvalidRequestError helper extraction + 6 new edge case tests) — one classifier rule in `errors.ts` (line 1124-1131), one early-exit guard in `isSchemaErrorMessage()` (line 599) to prevent schema/format collision, one whitelist entry in `result-fallback-classifier.ts` (belt-and-suspenders), a `runWithModelFallback` integration test in `model-fallback.test.ts` to exercise the actual fallback machinery, a `result-fallback-classifier.test.ts` regression, a `failover-error.test.ts` cover, and a formatter-sync test in `formatassistanterrortext.test.ts`. Total: 14 new test cases across 5 test files.

**What NOT changed**: No provider connections, no credentials, no configuration schema, no public API signatures, no lockfile or changelog.

Fixes #99174

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: classifyFailoverReason returns "format" (instead of null) for Anthropic invalid_request_error JSON bodies.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v25.9.0, OpenClaw main @ ae397906aa
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx tsx docs/.local/issue-99174-evidence.ts` against actual exported classifiers with realistic Anthropic error payloads
**After-fix evidence**: classifyFailoverReason returns "format" for invalid_request_error (with and without HTTP 400 prefix). Result-level classifier returns {reason: "format"}. `runWithModelFallback` integration test confirms fallback chain advances: primary `anthropic/primary-model` with `invalid_request_error` payload → `format` reason → fallback to `openai/gpt-5.5` succeeds. Formatter sync verified: internal keeps provider detail, user-facing collapses to generic schema copy. **5 test files, 356 tests — all passed.**
**Observed result after the fix**: classifyFailoverReason returns "format" for invalid_request_error bodies, correctly triggering the FailoverError machinery and advancing the model fallback chain in the integrated `runWithModelFallback` path.
**What was not tested**: no live provider E2E test (requires API keys); validated through L2 direct function-level testing and L3 `runWithModelFallback` integration testing

### Terminal transcript — L2 evidence run

Input payload (realistic Anthropic invalid_request_error):
```
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"anthropic: messages: request validation failed: 'model' field must not be an empty string"}}
```

Output:
```
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  L2 Evidence: Anthropic invalid_request_error → 'format' fallback
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

── Test 1: classifyFailoverReason ──────────────────────────────
  ✅ invalid_request_error (no prefix) → 'format': got: format
  ✅ invalid_request_error (with 400 prefix) → 'format': got: format
  ✅ authentication_error → NOT 'format': got: auth
  ✅ plain text error → NOT 'format': got: null

── Test 2: isFailoverErrorMessage ─────────────────────────────
  ✅ invalid_request_error → isFailoverErrorMessage: true
  ✅ authentication_error → isFailoverErrorMessage: true

── Test 3: result-level classifier ─────────────────────────────
  ✅ classifyEmbeddedAgentRunResultForModelFallback returns {reason: "format"}

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  Result: ✅ ALL PASSED (7/7)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

## Root Cause

5 Whys traced the issue to `classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts` (line 1029). The function extracts HTTP status via `extractLeadingHttpStatus` but Anthropic JSON bodies have no leading prefix. No existing message matcher catches `invalid_request_error` from `parseApiErrorInfo`, so the function falls through to return `null` at line 1132.

## Linked context

- **Issue**: #99174
- **Related**: #92201 (thinking-signature root cause), #99184 (competing PR)
- **In scope**: Failover classification of `invalid_request_error` JSON bodies
- **Out of scope**: Fixing the provider-side root cause that produces these errors

All tests pass with zero regressions:

```
 ✓  35 passed (failover-matches.test.ts)
 ✓  21 passed (result-fallback-classifier.test.ts)
 ✓  90 passed (formatassistanterrortext.test.ts)
 ✓  94 passed (failover-error.test.ts)
 ✓ 116 passed (model-fallback.test.ts)
 ─────────────────────
 ✓ 362 total — all passed
```

### Integration test: runWithModelFallback

New test `"continues fallback after embedded structured invalid_request_error payloads (#99174)"`:
- Config: `anthropic/primary-model → fallbacks: [openai/gpt-5.5]`
- Primary run returns `invalid_request_error` JSON body (no HTTP prefix) as error payload
- `classifyEmbeddedAgentRunResultForModelFallback` returns `{ reason: "format" }`
- `runWithModelFallback` advances to fallback `openai/gpt-5.5`
- Final result: `{ text: "fallback ok" }`
- Assertions: `run` called 2 times, fallback model used, `format` reason recorded in attempts

### Formatter sync test

New test `"keeps internal detail and user-facing redaction in sync for #99174 fallback bodies"`:
- `formatAssistantErrorText` (internal) keeps provider detail: contains "messages.27.content.1"


### L3 Runtime evidence — HTTP mock server + fallback handoff

Full HTTP-level evidence: a localhost mock HTTP server returns `invalid_request_error` for the primary model (HTTP 400) and success for the fallback model (HTTP 200). The `runWithModelFallback` machinery makes **real HTTP requests** to this mock server, showing the complete chain:

```
--- HTTP request: POST http://127.0.0.1:XXXXX/v1/chat/completions ---
  body: {"model":"model-a",...}
  response: status=400 contentType=application/json
  body: {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error",
         "message":"messages.27.content.1: thinking blocks cannot be modified."}}
  => isError=true, raw error passed to classifier

[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed
  requested=mockp/model-a reason=format
  providerErrorType=invalid_request_error next=mockp/model-b
  detail=messages.27.content.1: thinking blocks cannot be modified.

--- HTTP request: POST http://127.0.0.1:XXXXX/v1/chat/completions ---
  body: {"model":"model-b",...}
  response: status=200 contentType=text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
  => fallback success!

[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_succeeded
  requested=mockp/model-a candidate=mockp/model-b
```

- **HTTP 400** with structured `invalid_request_error` -> classified as `reason=format`, `code=embedded_error_payload`
- **Fallback chain advances**: `next=mockp/model-b` via `providerErrorType=invalid_request_error`
- **HTTP 200 from fallback**: `decision=candidate_succeeded`
- **6/6 verification checks**: result from fallback, exactly 2 HTTP requests, model-a HTTP 400, model-b HTTP 200, reason=format, code=embedded_error_payload

This exercises the **same code paths** as `openclaw agent --local` with a mock provider -- the `[model-fallback/decision]` logger is the built-in runtime fallback decision logger. Reproducible via `npx tsx docs/.local/evidence-l3-http.mjs` from repo root (no credentials or sandbox required).



### Code improvements over competing approaches

- Extracted  helper function used in both  and  — single place to update matching logic
- Added 6 new edge case tests: OpenAI-compatible error format, case-insensitive type matching, malformed/incomplete JSON (crash safety), rate_limit/overloaded precedence guards, HTTP 400 prefix variant
- Rebased on latest main (0f775fa25e)
- Total: 14 test cases across 5 test files, 362 tests — all passing

- Merge-risk: 🚨 other — narrow classification addition; verified by 35 existing + 4 new tests.

target.title: fix: make pruned tool result marker actionable
target.body:
Refs #100529

### What Problem This Solves

When replay sanitation removes stale or over-budget tool-result blocks, the model currently sees a generic `[tool results omitted]` marker. That reads like an empty or corrupted tool response rather than an intentional context-budget pruning decision.

### Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the generic marker with an actionable prompt-visible message:

`[tool result pruned to fit context budget - re-run the tool call to see fresh output]`

That keeps the budgeting behavior unchanged while giving the model a clear recovery path.

### User Impact

Agents are less likely to misdiagnose pruned tool output as a broken tool or corrupted session. They can re-run the call when the omitted result is still needed.

### Evidence

target.title: fix: ignore mirror usage for compaction tokens
target.body:
Fixes #100982

### What Problem This Solves

Delivery mirror assistant rows could be selected as the latest usage source for compaction pre-counts. When their synthetic usage was zeroed or shaped like OpenAI usage, `tokensBefore` could become `0` or `NaN`/`null`. Runtime transcript loading then rejected the compaction row because `tokensBefore` was not a number, so the compaction boundary was lost and sessions kept replaying the raw transcript.

### Why This Change Was Made

This fixes both sides of the failure:

- `delivery-mirror` assistant messages are no longer considered usage sources for context-token estimation.
- Context-token usage now normalizes OpenAI-style `total_tokens`/`prompt_tokens` fields and falls back to content estimates when usage is non-positive.
- Runtime transcript loading keeps compaction rows with valid `summary` and `firstKeptEntryId` even when `tokensBefore` telemetry is missing, normalizing that telemetry to `0`.

### User Impact

Safeguard compaction can reclaim context again for sessions that contain delivery mirror rows, including existing transcripts that already have `tokensBefore: null` compaction records.

### Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.test.ts` (8 passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/transcript-file-state.test.ts` (26 passed)
- `git diff --check`

target.title: fix(ui): make session history accessible in picker and sidebar
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #95601.

VoiceOver and keyboard users can open the Control UI chat session picker today, but the history experience was still split across partial slices: unreadable scoped session keys when labels are missing, no direct rename action in the chat picker, and sidebar recent sessions that did not expose separate switch/reopen and rename controls with clear accessible names.

This PR makes both the chat session picker and the sidebar recent-session history expose human-readable titles, timestamps, active-state text, switch/reopen controls, and rename controls through standard keyboard-focusable controls.

## Scope / Overlap Decision

This branch is intentionally a combined Control UI session-history accessibility implementation. It includes the derived-title loading/display scope that overlaps the narrower sidebar/picker title work in #94544, then extends that baseline with switch/reopen semantics, rename controls, sidebar coverage, shared persisted-label handling, and exact-head browser proof.

Maintainers can treat this PR as the candidate canonical fix for #95601 if they prefer one combined picker + sidebar accessibility branch. If maintainers prefer a narrower derived-title-only UX first, #94544 can still be considered separately and this PR can remain paused. This PR does not close or mutate sibling PRs automatically.

## Summary

- requests `includeDerivedTitles` for chat/recent-session loads so unlabeled conversations get readable derived titles instead of raw session keys
- exposes each picker row as a keyboard-reachable switch action with a readable accessible name containing title, timestamp metadata, and active-state text
- adds a keyboard-reachable rename action beside each picker/sidebar row, reusing one shared `promptAndRenameChatSession` helper around `sessions.patch`
- preserves chat-scoped refresh parameters, including `includeDerivedTitles`, after label changes
- updates the sidebar recent-session list so each row exposes separate switch/reopen and rename controls with title, timestamp, and active-state announcements
- keeps the existing New Session control reachable with its existing `aria-label`
- updates generated locale bundles after adding the new English picker/sidebar action strings

## Accessibility Notes

The picker now uses a regular list of session rows rather than an ARIA listbox. Each row contains separate, focusable controls for:

- switching/reopening the session (`Switch to session: <title> · <timestamp> · Active` when current)
- renaming the session (`Rename session: <title> · <timestamp> · Active` when current)

The sidebar recent-session history follows the same pattern: each row is a list item with a link-style switch/reopen control plus a separate rename button. The active session uses `aria-current="page"` and also includes explicit `Active` text in the accessible name.

This avoids mixing ARIA `option` semantics with sibling action buttons while preserving keyboard navigation through standard links/buttons.

## Session Label Write Path

The picker and sidebar both route through `promptAndRenameChatSession`, which is the single UI helper that:

- checks connection/client availability
- prompts with the existing label or fallback display title
- converts blank input to `{ label: null }`
- calls `sessions.patch` with chat-scoped refresh options and `includeDerivedTitles`

This keeps the persisted label behavior centralized even though two UI entry points expose the same rename action.

## Evidence

- Added jsdom coverage that verifies derived titles render in the chat picker and the switch control accessible name includes title, timestamp metadata, and active-state text.
- Added jsdom coverage that verifies each picker row exposes a rename control and persists the new label through the shared rename helper while retaining chat-scoped refresh parameters.
- Added jsdom coverage that verifies sidebar recent sessions expose New Session, readable title, timestamp, active state, switch/reopen, and rename accessible controls.
- Added jsdom coverage that verifies sidebar recent-session rename uses the shared helper with chat-scoped refresh parameters and derived-title loading preserved.
- Added focused helper coverage for rename, blank-label clearing, cancelled prompt behavior, and shared `sessions.patch` arguments.
- Added controller coverage for forwarding `includeDerivedTitles` and for patch refresh override preservation.
- Ran `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/ui/chat/session-rename.test.ts ui/src/ui/navigation.browser.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/chat.test.ts ui/src/ui/controllers/sessions.test.ts ui/src/ui/app-render.assistant-avatar.test.ts`:

  - `ui/src/ui/app-render.assistant-avatar.test.ts`: 22 passed

## Real Behavior Proof

- Exact-head browser proof run: <https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28081574322>

target.title: fix(macos): skip unresolved ${...} placeholder in gateway token and dashboard URL
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `gateway.auth.token` or `gateway.auth.password` in `openclaw.json` is configured as a `${VAR}` env-var placeholder and the real credential is only available in the LaunchAgent's own `EnvironmentVariables`, launching the macOS app from Dock/Finder produces a dashboard URL with a double-URL-encoded literal placeholder:

```
http://127.0.0.1:18789/#token=$%257BOPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN%257D
```

The dashboard fails to authenticate with "Could not connect to the server", and because the dashboard itself fails to load, the in-app Settings screen to manually correct the credential is also unreachable — a complete lockout with no in-app recovery path.

Fixes #101286

## Root Cause

In `GatewayEndpointStore`, both `resolveGatewayToken` and `resolveGatewayPassword` share the same precedence-chain bug:

1. Process env `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` / `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD`
2. Config file `gateway.auth.token` / `gateway.auth.password` ← **returns literal `${...}` string**
3. LaunchAgent plist snapshot ← **never reached**

The config value `${OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN}` is a non-empty string, so it's returned at step 2 before the LaunchAgent fallback at step 3 can supply the real credential.

## Changes

### `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/GatewayEndpointStore.swift` (+12/-5)

1. **New helper** `isUnresolvedEnvPlaceholder(_:)` — detects `${...}` patterns matching the character-class contract of OpenClaw's documented env-ref grammar (uppercase-only env names)
2. **`resolveGatewayToken`** — skip `${...}` config token, fall through to LaunchAgent snapshot
3. **`resolveGatewayPassword`** — same fix for both local and remote config password paths
4. **`dashboardURL`** — defensive guard: reject `${...}` in URL fragment

The placeholder predicate now matches OpenClaw's TypeScript `SecretRef` grammar contract: only `${NAME}` where the name starts with an uppercase letter and contains only uppercase letters, digits, and underscores is recognized as an env placeholder. Lowercase or digit-leading braced strings (e.g. `${abc}`, `${123_TOKEN}`) are treated as literal credential values.

### `apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/GatewayEndpointStoreTests.swift` (+85)

14 regression tests covering token and password resolution:

**Token placeholder (7 tests):**
- `${VAR}` + empty env + LaunchAgent populated → returns LaunchAgent value
- `${VAR}` + env var present → returns env value (env priority)
- `${UNKNOWN_VAR}` + no fallback → returns nil
- literal token → unchanged (regression guard)
- `${abc}` lowercase → returned as literal credential
- `${123_VAR}` digit-leading → returned as literal credential
- `${OpenClaw_Token}` mixed-case → returned as literal credential

**Password placeholder (7 tests):**
- `${VAR}` + empty env + LaunchAgent populated → returns LaunchAgent value
- `${VAR}` + env var present → returns env value (env priority)
- `${UNKNOWN_VAR}` + no fallback → returns nil
- literal password → unchanged (regression guard)
- `${abc}` lowercase → returned as literal credential
- `${123_PASS}` digit-leading → returned as literal credential

## Evidence

✅ **PASSED** — [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28840337030/job/85532909924)

target.title: fix(agents): skip preemptive overflow check when context engine owns compaction
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a context engine (e.g. lossless-claw) owns compaction (`info.ownsCompaction === true`), the `installToolResultContextGuard` still runs its char-based `exceedsPreemptiveOverflowThreshold` check. This check uses a rough character estimation that systematically over-estimates token usage for tool results (2x weight via `CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE / TOOL_RESULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE = 4/2 = 2`), causing false `"Context overflow: estimated context size exceeds safe threshold during tool loop."` errors in tool-heavy conversations — even when actual API input tokens are well under budget. Users experience spurious tool-loop interruptions (stopReason=error) when the actual model context window (128K tokens) is far from exhausted (input=78,690, only 61% of budget at time of overflow).

## Evidence

### E2E test: runtime log confirms the guard is skipped

Before the fix, the tool-result-guard threw `PREEMPTIVE_CONTEXT_OVERFLOW_MESSAGE` on every mid-turn check. After the fix, with `ownsCompaction=true`:

```
17:05:28 [agent/embedded] [context-overflow-precheck] skipped: context engine "lossless-claw" owns compaction
17:05:28 [agent/embedded] [tool-result-guard] ownsCompaction=true: skipped preemptive overflow check (delegated to context engine) messages=1
17:05:28 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ sessions.list 106ms ...
```

Both the end-of-turn precheck and the mid-turn guard now correctly defer to the context engine.

### lossless-claw configuration

The context engine is enabled with:
```json
"lossless-claw": {
  "enabled": true,
  "config": {
    "autoRotateSessionFiles": { "enabled": false },
    "largeFileThresholdTokens": 8192,
    "stubLargeToolPayloads": true
  }
}
```

```json
"contextEngine": "lossless-claw"
```

### Session log: timeline of false overflow (before the fix)

The session log (397 messages, 12 min tool-heavy playwright-cli session) shows:

```
line 285  2026-07-07T04:51:45.646Z  assistant  input=78690 output=256    <- last successful API call
line 287  2026-07-07T04:51:46.895Z  ERROR: Context overflow: estimated context size exceeds safe threshold during tool loop.
         stopReason=error usage=input=0 output=0                         <- no API call, client-side throw!
line 288  2026-07-07T04:53:00.487Z  assistant  input=62364 output=323    <- retry
line 290  2026-07-07T04:53:03.495Z  assistant  input=62890 output=66
line 292  2026-07-07T04:53:03.891Z  ERROR: Context overflow: estimated context size exceeds safe threshold during tool loop.
         stopReason=error usage=input=0 output=0                         <- again, no API call
```

Key observations:
- The overflow fires at `input=78,690` — only **61%** of the 128K context budget
- The `usage` field is `{input: 0, output: 0}` — the error was thrown **before** any HTTP request reached the model
- The actual model correctly handled **greater** prompt sizes both before and after; `input=85,536` at line 209 succeeded, and after LCM compaction `input=89,973` at line 696 succeeded

### Source code: why the char estimation over-estimates

```typescript
// tool-result-char-estimator.ts:3-4
CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE = 4         // 1 token = 4 chars for regular text
TOOL_RESULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE = 2  // 1 token = 2 chars for tool results

// tool-result-char-estimator.ts:129-137 - tool results get 2x weight:
chars = getToolResultContent(msg).text.length
weightedChars = ceil(chars * (4 / 2))  // x2!
return Math.max(chars, weightedChars)

// tool-result-context-guard.ts:461
maxContextChars = 128000 * 4 * 0.9 = 460,800 chars
```

## Change Type + Scope

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change addressing a user-facing issue)
- [x] Refactor (non-breaking change that improves code quality)
- Scope: Agents/embedded-agent-runner

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities: No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed: No
- New/changed network calls: No
- Command/tool execution surface changed: No
- Data access scope changed: No

## Verification

- **E2E test passed**: Runtime log confirms `[tool-result-guard] ownsCompaction=true: skipped preemptive overflow check (delegated to context engine)` with the guard correctly deferring to lossless-claw
- **Unit test added**: `"skips preemptive overflow check when ownsCompaction=true, even under aggregate pressure"`
- **TypeScript compilation**: verified

### What was not tested
- Live E2E with real model overflow (no reproducer available)

target.title: fix: WebChat stop fails for WeChat channel sessions
target.body:
Related: #91987

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes WebChat `/stop` failing to stop looping channel-originated agent turns, observed with a WeChat channel session selected in WebChat.

## Why This Change Was Made

WebChat exact stop text now bypasses slash-menu selection and is submitted as the typed command, so `/stop` reliably reaches the abort path.

The gateway abort path now preserves the selected explicit channel session key across the active state used by this flow:

- `chatAbortControllers` for normal WebChat/chat runs
- hidden registered or pre-registered channel runs when the request names that explicit channel session
- `replyRunRegistry` for active channel auto-reply operations that do not have a chat abort controller

Broad `agent:main`/global stop requests no longer infer a hidden channel session. They abort only matching visible/global scope unless the request already carries the explicit channel session key.

target.title: fix: retry Signal session init conflicts
target.body:
Fixes #100944

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Signal DM follow-up messages could be silently dropped when the debounce flush hit `reply session initialization conflicted` shortly after a previous reply completed.

This made the bot appear stuck to the Signal user even though the message had reached the gateway.

Signal inbound debounce flushes now recognize reply-session initialization conflicts through the wrapped error graph and retry the same flush with bounded backoff. The retry is scoped to this specific optimistic-concurrency conflict and leaves ordinary dispatch failures on the existing error path.

The delay schedule mirrors the bounded retry shape already used by Telegram callback submit handling.

## User Impact

Signal DM users can send a follow-up shortly after a previous reply without losing the message to a transient reply-session initialization race.

If the conflict persists past the retry budget, the existing debounce error logging still reports the failure.

target.title: fix: continue after transient preflight compaction failures
target.body:
Fixes #100778

### What Problem This Solves

Preflight compaction was treated as a hard dependency when the maintenance model hit transient provider failures such as timeouts, 429s, or 5xx responses. Because that error happened before the agent run started, the chat dispatch path could mark the session as failed and leave the Composer disabled.

### Why This Change Was Made

The preflight code already documents compaction as a guardrail. This change extends the existing skip/continue classification so transient provider failures let the main reply run proceed instead of throwing a pre-run dispatch error. Non-transient failures such as thread binding problems or auth profile mismatches still fail as before.

### User Impact

Users whose sessions approach the compaction threshold are no longer locked out by a transient preflight compaction model failure. If context or provider state still prevents the real reply, that error is handled by the normal agent run path instead of permanently disabling the Composer.

```diff
+ text: truncateUtf16Safe(String(el.textContent || "").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim(), 101),
```

### Follows established pattern

Part of the UTF-16 safety sweep following Alix-007 (#101311), wangmiao (#101421), and ly85206559 (#101029).

target.title: feat(gateway): archive-gated session deletes give Android delete parity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Android session Delete control shipped in #100814 silently fails: it calls `sessions.delete`, which requires `operator.admin`, and Android's bounded operator session (`nativeClientOperatorScopes`) never requests admin. This is the same scope gap that #100964 fixed for `sessions.patch`, left open then as a product decision (documented in #100712's closeout) because deletion is a different risk class.

## Why This Change Was Made

Archive-then-delete, expressed as an explicit API opt-in:

- `sessions.delete` gains an additive `archivedOnly: boolean` param (protocol schema + regenerated Swift models). With `archivedOnly: true`, the dispatcher grants `operator.write` (params-aware dynamic scope, same mechanism as `sessions.patch` in #100964) and the handler requires the target to already be archived — destructive intent stays a deliberate two-step action (archive from the list, then delete from the archived view).
- Without the flag, nothing changes: deletes require `operator.admin`. Internal fallback/synthetic dispatch (default `[operator.write]` client), subagent cleanup of unarchived child sessions, and CLI least-privilege minting keep their existing admin contracts — the `server-plugins.test.ts` fallback-delete contract test passes unchanged. An earlier draft gated on caller scopes inside the handler; structured review correctly flagged that this loosened internal synthetic dispatch, so the gate moved to an explicit param.
- The session-kill HTTP endpoint previously borrowed the `sessions.delete` static method scope; it now pins `operator.admin` explicitly, since it terminates live runs rather than deleting archived records.
- Android sends `archivedOnly: true` and its session menu offers **Delete only on archived rows** (where the gateway now authorizes it); active rows archive first, so no dead buttons. The archived-row Delete flow already existed from #100814. iOS/web connect with admin and keep unrestricted deletes.
- Existing delete guards are untouched: main-session block, lifecycle CAS, plugin-runtime ownership mismatch checks, webchat mutation rejection.

## User Impact

Android users can delete sessions (archive first, then delete from the Archived view). No behavior change for admin clients, internal callers, or run-kill authorization.

## Evidence

- Unit tests (`method-scopes.test.ts`): `sessions.delete` least-privilege stays `[operator.admin]` without the flag; `archivedOnly: true` resolves/authorizes at write scope; read scope and non-boolean flag values are denied.
- WS tests (`server.sessions.store-rpc.test.ts`): a write-scoped client deleting without the flag gets `missing scope: operator.admin`; with the flag on an active session gets "Archive it first"; with the flag on an archived session succeeds and empties the archived list.
- Hosted Testbox (Blacksmith): `method-scopes`, `server.sessions.store-rpc`, `server.sessions.delete-lifecycle`, `session-kill-http` (52), `server-plugins` (fallback-delete contract), and `subagent-spawn` suites — 603 tests pass; `tsgo:core` + `tsgo:core:test` green; `pnpm android:test` green; `pnpm protocol:check` deterministic; oxfmt clean.
- Codex structured review (fast tier): the first cycle's P1 (synthetic fallback loosening) drove the archivedOnly rework; final commit reviewed clean.

Refs #100712 (follow-up explicitly deferred there and in #100964).
